2_Introduction: The device shows the highest PCE of 15.61% with a VOC of 1.0118 V, a JSC of 20.77 mA/cm², and an FF of 74.28%. For the Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1, 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solution was prepared. Afterwards, the perovskite precursor solution was deposited on the substrate via a two-step spin coating process; first, the solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 30 s. At 6 s before the end of the second step, 160 µL of CB was drop-coated to treat the perovskite films. The resulting wet perovskite films were annealed at 110 °C for 25 min. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at around 12.65°, with an intensity of 2107.57 cts and a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 0.21, which corresponds to the characteristic peak of PbI₂. The relatively low intensity of this peak suggests a limited presence of residual PbI₂.
3_Result_Discussion: The triple-cation mixed-halide perovskite composition (Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1) is engineered to balance the tolerance factor and bandgap, with bromine incorporation enhancing phase stability and suppressing halide ion migration, while the high precursor concentration (1.73 M) and optimized two-step spin-coating process—featuring a critical chlorobenzene antisolvent drip at 6 seconds before the end of the second, high-speed (5000 rpm) step—collectively govern the crystallization kinetics by rapidly triggering supersaturation and modulating solvent evaporation to foster dense, uniform nucleation and subsequent grain growth during the 110 °C anneal, thus minimizing pinhole formation and bulk defect densities. This meticulous crystallization control is structurally corroborated by the XRD analysis, where the characteristically low intensity (2107.57 cts) and narrow full width at half maximum (0.21°) of the residual PbI₂ peak at ~12.65° confirm the high phase purity, suppressed secondary phases, and reduced microstrain within the perovskite lattice, which collectively indicate effective suppression of deep-level defects and non-radiative recombination pathways, thereby facilitating efficient charge extraction. The resultant high-quality photoactive layer, in conjunction with the optimized interfacial contacts, ultimately delivers a power conversion efficiency of 15.61% with a VOC of 1.0118 V, a JSC of 20.77 mA/cm², and an FF of 74.28%.
